newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Five soldiers killed in Colombian rebel attack.
newsitem.headline: Five soldiers killed in Colombian rebel attack.

text.p: The death toll from a rebel attack on a military base in northwest Colombia rose to five on Friday after one of six soldiers wounded in the assault died, authorities said.
Military spokesmen said guerrillas continued to wreak havoc with transportation across the province overnight, setting 19 vehicles ablaze as part of a bid to shut down two key highways.
Attacks on vehicles followed a similar rash of vandalism on Tuesday night when rebels torched at least 11 trucks and buses on the main highway linking Medellin, the capital of Antioquia, to Bogota.

The attack on the Heroes de Barbacoas counterinsurgency base in a mountainous area about 40 miles (65 km) east of Medellin occurred before dawn on Thursday. The base, guarded by just 28 soliders, was completely overrun by a combined force of about 150 Revolutionary Armed Forces of Colombia (FARC) and National Liberation Army (ELN) rebels.

A 22-year-old solider identified as Jhon Mario Segura died in a Medellin hospitl of injuries he suffered in the attack on Thursday night, raising the number of soldiers killed to five, army spokesmen said. They said at least six other troops had been killed in fighting raging since Tuesday in the banana-growing region of Uraba in the northwest corner of Antioquia near the border with Panama.
Police said the bullet-riddled bodies of two other soldiers were discovered on Thursday, along with those of two civilians, dumped in a rural area outside the Caribbean port of Santa Marta.
The FARC and ELN, both Marxist-led groups, have been waging war against the state since the 1960s.
